extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys, PTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline / disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for evaluating whether a patent practitioner acted with reasonable diligence, promptness, communication, and billing/professional conduct in preparing and filing patent applications under 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 and related professional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client. 'Reasonable ... when used in relation to conduct by a practitioner means the conduct of a reasonably prudent and competent practitioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess timeliness of preparation and filing (e.g., prolonged multi-month delay to prepare/file a provisional application). Consider objective measures (typical time to complete a provisional ~20 hours cited) and actual hours billed. Case examples: repeated missed deadlines/promises and failure to file despite client follow-ups support finding of lack of diligence. Procrastination and delay are flagged as professional misconduct in precedent (quoting In re Exley and other disciplinary cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for delays caused by poor communication and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner bears responsibility when work is delayed because he did not reliably and timely convey communications among himself, the draftsman, and the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate evidence of missed/late communications (unreturned emails, unanswered inquiries, failure to forward drafts), timing of draft/drawing completions (e.g., drawings completed two months after engagement), and whether the practitioner coordinated necessary third parties. Lack of timely communication among participants is an independent factor supporting a finding of unreasonable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to refrain from accepting representation that impairs competent/diligent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys have a duty to refrain from accepting representation if doing so will impair the attorney's ability to provide competent representation, to act with reasonable diligence, and to keep the client reasonably informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider practitioner’s existing workload/commitments (e.g., full-time employment, long commute, limited daytime access to materials) and whether accepting the matter under those conditions made adequate performance unlikely. If the practitioner knew or should have known representation would be impaired, accepting the matter weighs against reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep client reasonably informed and respond promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep clients reasonably informed and act with reasonable punctuality and promptness in advancing the client's interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for patterns of non-response to repeated client inquiries (emails/phone calls), failure to provide promised drafts, and lack of status updates. Repeated silence or late, excuse-based replies supports disciplinary concern. Timely responses are more critical where client circumstances create urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of particular circumstances in evaluating diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether conduct was diligent must account for particular circumstances of the representation, including agreements between client and practitioner about scope, division of labor, and cost-saving arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess facts such as the client agreeing to provide descriptive drafting, acceptance of off-hours work, and cost-saving choices. These contextual facts may mitigate but do not excuse unreasonable delay, poor communication, or failure to produce work product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness measured against client's specific needs and harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence must be measured in light of the client's needs; efficiency is especially significant when client faces financial hardship or has time-sensitive business plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider client's stated urgency (e.g., need to file to pursue bids, crowdfunding, employment concerns) and whether delays materially harmed client's opportunities. Greater client vulnerability or time-sensitivity increases practitioner obligation to be prompt and communicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and adherence to fee arrangements (billing practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must honor fee arrangements (e.g., flat-fee agreements) and provide transparent billing; attempts to extract additional fees inconsistent with agreed terms are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether practitioner respected flat-fee terms, provided itemized bills upon request, and avoided coercive or confusing demands for 'overages.' Threatening to charge for an itemized bill or implying a flat fee will be exceeded without prior agreement is an anti-pattern indicating poor professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client access to work product and right to copies
rubrics_metrics.description: A client who has paid for work is entitled to copies of the practitioner's work product (drafts of applications) upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding drafts or refusing to provide a client's file (after full payment) supports finding of misconduct; repeated demands by client for drafts and the practitioner's failure to deliver are relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and candor in communications about work status
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must be truthful about the status of work; misrepresentations that drafts were sent or that matters are '100 percent finished' when not true are disciplinary concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess statements to client (promises to send drafts, representations that work was finished) against documentary evidence (email logs, drafts actually produced). Repeated false assurances or excuses (computer hacked, lost power) that contradict contemporaneous records undermine credibility and support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective time/effort benchmarks in assessing reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks (e.g., typical hours to complete a provisional application) can inform whether claimed time/effort was reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare practitioner's own estimates (e.g., 'usually about 20 hours') and billed or claimed hours (e.g., 35 hours for both design and utility) with the observed delays and work produced. Large disparities between time spent and expected output can indicate failure to act diligently.
